URL: https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-september-30-2026/
Institute for the Study of War (ISW) — Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, 30 September 2026. Confirmed live and dated 30 September 2026 (it was 404 at 19:10 BST on 30 Sep; published overnight). Authors on the Critical Threats mirror: Kateryna Shymkiv, Nikolai Sundstrom and George Barros.

KEY TAKEAWAYS (verbatim):
1. Russia conducted a massive combined drone and missile strike against Ukraine on the night of September 29 to 30, primarily targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv City and marking the beginning of Russia's strike campaign aimed at degrading Ukraine's energy security ahead of Winter 2026-2027 and forcing Ukraine to capitulate.
2. Russia notably began its Winter 2026-2027 strike campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure ahead of Ukraine's heating season, as Russian President Vladimir Putin likely recently adopted a modified theory of victory that relies on Russia's long-range strike campaign to force Ukraine to surrender over Winter 2026-2027.
3. A likely Russian drone violated Moldovan airspace and crashed near Hirbovat, Anenii Noi, on the morning of September 30.
4. The Kremlin is signaling its intention to use the seizure of assets belonging to European companies operating in Russia and to hold such companies' assets hostage in order to coerce European states into reconsidering their sanctions policies against Russia.
5. Ukrainian forces recently advanced north of Sumy City.
6. Russian forces launched an unspecified number of Zircon or Onyx anti-ship cruise missiles, an unspecified number of Iskander-M or S-400 ballistic missiles, and 188 drones against Ukraine overnight on September 29 to 30; and 285 drones, an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, and several Banderol or Dan-T loitering munitions during the day on September 30.

NAMED QUOTES / ATTRIBUTED DETAIL:
- Zelensky (30 Sep): Russian forces launched nearly 190 strike drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles against Ukraine overnight, primarily targeting Kyiv City and Kyiv Oblast energy infrastructure.
- Ukrainian PM Serhiy Koretskyi: the strike package was "the largest combined strike package targeting Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the end of the last heating season" (roughly early April 2026).
- Ukraine's Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko: Winter 2026-2027 could be the "hardest and the harshest winter" of the war thus far.
- Kravchenko also: each hour of a missile alert costs Ukraine an estimated $45 million because alerts halt economic activity; Russian strikes have caused an estimated $10 billion in damage to fixed assets in 2026, including steel plants, warehouses, logistics infrastructure and data centres; sirens last up to 10 hours a day.
- Ukrainian state energy company Centrenergo reported on 30 September that Russian strikes damaged the Trypillya Thermal Power Plant in Kyiv Oblast.
- Ukrenergo introduced emergency power outages in Kyiv Oblast; outages also reported in Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv and Sumy oblasts.
- The Russian MoD claimed Russian forces struck the Kyivska electrical substation, the Kyiv Hydroelectric Power Plant and a battery energy storage park in Kyiv Oblast.
- Air Force detail: 188 Shahed-type (86 jet-powered) and Gerbera-type strike drones plus Parodiya decoys overnight 29-30 Sep; 5 missiles and 155 drones downed; strikes at 18 locations. Then 285 drones (174 jet-powered) during the day on 30 Sep, 254 downed, 146 of them jet-powered.
- ISW assessment: Putin is likely beginning the systematic campaign before Ukraine can protect its grid or develop countermeasures to ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, and is attempting to demoralise the population and force surrender before meaningful peace negotiations.
